subject: Service guarantee exception and MSA / order form coordination
messages:
From: Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@medivance.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soriano <elena.s@medivance.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:04:00-04:00
Subject: Request: custom service guarantee / availability exception and MSA redlines

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the standard Redwood MSA and order form and have two asks before Procurement can approve: a) an explicit addendum for a tailored availability guarantee (we're requesting a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment with a defined incident credit formula) and b) clarified order form language that captures latency SLOs for interactive endpoints (95th percentile under 200ms for our production traffic profile).

Attached are our redlines and a short spreadsheet showing expected TPS and latency distribution (Attachments: MDV_MSA_Redlines.pdf, Medivance_SLA_Req.xlsx). We'd like to understand if Redwood can provide an exception addendum and what the escalations & credits would look like. Also please advise whether Redwood requires a separate Dedicated commitment or if hosted options can be covered under the proposed order form language.

Can we get a view by EOD Friday? We're operating on a constrained renewal calendar.

Thanks,
Tim O'Neill
Sr. Procurement Manager
Medivance Health
Attachments: MDV_MSA_Redlines.pdf (PDF), Medivance_SLA_Req.xlsx (Excel)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom service guarantee / availability exception and MSA redlines

Ben/Marissa/Karthik —

Looping you in on a Medivance procurement ask. External attached redlines request a 99.95% uptime commitment and a 95th pctl latency SLO of 200ms for interactive endpoints. They also want the incident credit formula spelled out in the order form rather than buried in the SOW.

My suggested approach:
- Sales to confirm whether we can support the SLO on Hosted with autoscaling & prefix caching, or whether this requires Dedicated capacity (Ben).
- Sales Ops / Legal to review the proposed credit formula and suggest sanitized language for the order form (Marissa).
- Engineering to confirm feasibility and any caveats on latency SLOs tied to regional routing and burst behavior (Karthik).

I've drafted a short order form snippet below we can iterate on:

"Order Form — Service Guarantee (draft)"
"Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Service with 99.95% monthly availability (\"Availability SLO\") measured by successful request completion rates per calendar month. In the event Provider fails to meet the Availability SLO, Customer will be eligible for service credits calculated as: (Monthly Uptime Shortfall %) x (0.5% of monthly fees) for each 0.1% shortfall, capped at 50% of monthly service fees for the impacted product. Latency SLO for interactive endpoints: Provider will target 95th percentile request latency <= 200ms under normal production traffic conditions as described in the attached workload profile; latency credits are only applicable where Provider is the routing decision-maker and capacity is not impacted by customer-controlled configuration. Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures\"

Can you each take ownership of the pieces above? I'm planning to reply to Tim with a status by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (from customer) MDV_MSA_Redlines.pdf, Medivance_SLA_Req.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T17:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom service guarantee / availability exception and MSA redlines

Irene — I'll run an initial Hosted vs Dedicated feasibility check with infra and confirm any hard SLO blockers. Preliminary thoughts: 99.95% is doable on Dedicated; on Hosted we'd want clear traffic profiles and likely a short reserved burst window. I'll coordinate with Karthik and get back with a concrete recommendation and any cost delta.

Also attaching an internal redline of the order form snippet with Sales Ops language tweaks (Attachment: redlined_order_form.docx).

-Ben

Redwood Inference

From: Elena Soriano <elena.s@medivance.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@medivance.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom service guarantee / availability exception and MSA redlines

Thanks for the quick acknowledgement. Two clarifications from our side before you dive deeper:
1) Incident credit formula: we are open to a capped credit approach, but need a clearer definition of "monthly uptime shortfall" (is it measured across all endpoints or per-product?). We also want the credit calculation to be straightforward for our finance team.
2) SOC 2 evidence: Legal has asked for confirmation that Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is willing to provide the last SOC 2 report under NDA.

If you can confirm those points it will speed internal approvals.

Best,
Elena
Director, IT Procurement
Medivance Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tim O'Neill <tim.oneill@medivance.com>, Elena Soriano <elena.s@medivance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: custom service guarantee / availability exception and MSA redlines

Tim / Elena —

Quick update and next steps:
- Feasibility: Ben confirmed Dedicated will meet 99.95% with room for latency guarantees; Hosted may require a narrow guaranteed burst and region pinning. Karthik's note: latency SLOs are realistic for 95th pctl under test traffic; we will include a clause that credits apply only where Redwood controls routing and standard mitigations (caching/batching) are enabled.
- Incident credit clarifications (per Elena): we'll define "monthly uptime shortfall" as the percentage difference between the Availability SLO and measured successful request completion rate for the affected product group in a billing month; we'll add an example calculation in the order form.
- SOC 2: Marissa will send the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA — Marissa, can you confirm timeline?

Attached is our internal redlined Order Form snippet (redlined_order_form.docx) that reconciles your ask with our credit cap approach. I'm also attaching a DocuSign envelope link for the addendum once legal signs off: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/ABC123456789

If that looks ok to you, we'll route the final addendum to Legal for quick review and return a signed order form + addendum.

Thanks,
